en: Your phone says... debited. Eight hundred and forty rupees. The shopkeeper turns the speaker toward you — silence. Nothing came. And the queue behind you is getting louder.
So where is your money right now? It is not lost. It is stuck between two banks.
U-P-I moves about eighty crore payments a day. And the switch in the middle, run by N-P-C-I, gives each bank just fifteen seconds to answer.
Here is the path when everything works. You type your U-P-I pin. Your app sends the request to N-P-C-I. N-P-C-I asks your bank to debit you.
Your bank takes the money out of your account and replies, done.
Only then does N-P-C-I ask the shop's bank to credit the shop. The shop's bank adds the money and replies, done.
Two legs. A debit leg first, then a credit leg — two separate steps, on two separate bank computers. Your money leaves first... and arrives second.
Back to the counter. Your bank has already debited you. The credit request reaches the shop's bank... and the reply never comes back.
Maybe a network link dropped. Maybe the session timed out.
Fifteen seconds pass. N-P-C-I cannot wait forever, so it marks your payment as deemed — pending. Nobody knows yet whether the shop got the money.
So your app shows debited, and the shop shows nothing. Both screens are telling the truth.
Then the system checks itself. N-P-C-I goes back to the shop's bank and asks, what happened?
If the money reached the shop, it becomes a success. If it never reached, the shop's bank sends it back, and your bank reverses the debit. Either way, it has to settle.

So here is the rule. For a payment to a shop, the R-B-I says the money must come back within five days. Sent to a person, by the next day. If the bank is late, it owes you one hundred rupees for every day of delay — without you even asking.
Let me say that again. Shop, five days. Person, next day. Late means one hundred rupees a day.
And before you pay a second time... check the status of the first one.
That is the payment that breaks. So what happens in those few seconds when a hundred rupee payment goes right? Watch this next breakdown to find out.
